title: Distinct dynamics of conceptual and referential disruptions in human reading and large language model processing
abstract: arXiv:2608.25999v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Linguistic meaning is grounded in conceptual content, from which reference to particular entities emerges as words enter discourse. To examine the processing dynamics associated with these two dimensions of meaning, we selectively disrupted conceptual or referential information in short narratives and traced the resulting effects in human self-paced reading and in the predictive and representational processing of large language models. In human reading, conceptual disruptions produced a strong but localized processing cost, emerging immediately after the distorted word, reaching an early maximum, and then declining rapidly. Referential disruptions produced weaker effects, which decreased more gradually across subsequent words, and were more strongly modulated by sentence boundaries. translated_title: 人类阅读与大型语言模型处理中概念性干扰和指称性干扰的不同动态
translated_abstract: 语言意义植根于概念内容，当词语进入话语时，从中产生对特定实体的指称。为了考察与这两个意义维度相关的处理动态，我们在短篇叙事中选择性地干扰概念性或指称性信息，并追踪这些干扰在人类自定步速阅读以及大型语言模型的预测性和表征性处理中的影响。在人类阅读中，概念性干扰产生了强烈但局部的处理成本，在扭曲词后立即出现，达到早期峰值，然后迅速下降。指称性干扰产生的效应较弱，在后续词语中逐渐减弱，并受句子边界的调节更明显。在语言模型中，两种干扰均在操作词处立即出现。上下文模型惊讶度显示出与人类重新阅读模式密切平行的模式。
tldr: 本文揭示了人类阅读中概念性干扰引发强而短暂的处理成本，而指称性干扰产生弱而持久的效应，且大型语言模型表现出与人类不同的即时处理模式。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that conceptual disruptions cause strong but transient processing costs in human reading, while referential disruptions produce weaker and more persistent effects, with large language models showing distinct immediate processing patterns.
